NE Cali News Publication Area: How many H-1B petitions were made by employers classified under the Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services industry during 2025?
In 2025, one H-1B petition was filed by an employer classified under the Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services industry located within the NE Cali News publication area, as per data provided by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services via the H-1B Employer Data Hub.
Yongfei Enterprise Group Company, the only employer classified under the Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services industry the NE Cali News publication area to file an H-1B petition in 2025, had its petition approved, giving the company a 100% approval rate, according to data provided by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services via the H-1B Employer Data Hub.
Employers are classified under industries based on their reported operations and may be involved in multiple industries.
The H-1B visa program allows U.S. employers to temporarily employ foreign workers in specialty occupations that generally require highly specialized knowledge and at least a bachelor’s degree in a specific specialty, or its equivalent. Employers must pay H-1B workers at least the higher of the actual wage paid to similarly experienced and qualified employees or the prevailing wage for the occupation in the area of intended employment. These requirements protect H-1B employees and similarly employed U.S. workers.
The average approval rate for H-1B petitions across the United States in 2025 stood at 97.9%, slightly lower than 2024's 98%.
Compared to 2024, the Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services sector in the NE Cali News publication area saw a 50% decrease in the number of H-1B petitions during 2025.
Federal data show that about 1.32 million people obtained lawful permanent residence, or green cards, in fiscal year 2025, according to the Department of Homeland Security's Office of Homeland Security Statistics. Family-based categories accounted for 66.8% of the total, compared with 12.1% for employment-based categories. The H-1B program for specialty occupations and the H-2A program for seasonal agricultural work provide temporary work authorization; receiving one of those visas does not itself grant permanent residence.
In an August 2024 Pew Research Center survey, 46% of U.S. adults said legal immigration should remain at its current level. Asked separately which groups should receive top priority for legal immigration, 42% named highly skilled workers, 25% named people filling labor shortages, including agricultural workers, and 19% named people with close family in the U.S. Separately, family-based categories accounted for 66.8% of green cards granted in fiscal 2025, according to USAFacts' analysis of preliminary federal data.
Data in this article comes from the H-1B Employer Data Hub maintained by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. USCIS says information transferred manually from paper forms may contain missing or incorrect employer names, tax identification numbers or locations. Approval and denial totals reflect the agency’s first decision on each petition and exclude subsequent actions, such as appeals or revocations, and petitions pending when the data were generated.
